Your posting for a Senior Signal Processing Engineer describes work that lines up directly with what I have been doing at Fenno Radar Technologies for the past year and a half, and with the projects I built during my MSc at Kallavesi. Hannu Lehtonen

I am applying for the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position. Finland does not have many places where this concentration of signal processing and sensor engineering happens at scale, and Oulu is clearly one of them. It appeals to me as a place to build a career in this field.

What I have gained, though, is a thorough understanding of how a radar system fits together and where the interfaces between subsystems cause trouble. I have been through enough design reviews, fault investigations, and factory acceptance tests to know the architecture well, even though my personal contribution has been on the mechanical and systems side.

I expect my profile does not match every qualification in your posting, and I will not pretend otherwise. My degree is in mechanical engineering and my direct signal processing implementation experience is limited. What I can say is that five years inside a radar company have given me solid foundations and a clear direction: I want to transition into hands-on signal processing work, and I want to do it in an environment where I can learn from experienced engineers. I pick things up quickly when I am surrounded by the right kind of problems, and I am at a career stage where making this move matters more to me than staying where things are comfortable.

If there is a conversation worth having despite the gaps, I would welcome it.

Pawel Petrov

If you are open to considering someone who is still building her core technical depth but brings real operational experience and a genuine commitment to this domain, I would welcome the chance to talk.

Anneke Schneider

After eighteen years at Polaris RF Labs in Oulu, I have watched the city’s technology community grow from a handful of survivors of the Korvenmaa era into a genuine engineering cluster with its own identity. I am writing about the Senior Signal Processing Engineer position because I want to stay in this community — I have built my life here — but I also want a different kind of challenge within it.

My path into this field is unusual. I studied chemical engineering at SIT Bombay and moved to Finland in 2008 for personal reasons — my wife is from Oulu and we wanted to settle here. I know how to keep data infrastructure reliable, I understand the vocabulary and context of the domain even though I have not done the mathematics myself, and I have worked in an English-speaking technical environment for the entire duration of my career in Finland. Those are not the headline qualifications for this role and I know that, but they are genuine.

I follow Kaikuvaara’s work with real interest and I know several engineers who have moved between the RF and photonics companies in Oulu over the years. The community here is small enough that reputations travel, and Kaikuvaara has a good one. That matters to me after nearly two decades of watching which companies in this city people want to work at and which ones they quietly leave. The engineering culture is clearly strong, and it is something I want to be part of.

I recognise that my application may not be the strongest technical match. If there is any interest in discussing what I could contribute, I am available at short notice.

Matti Niemi

Kaikuvaara Oy
Oulu

Re: Senior Signal Processing Engineer

I have worked in optical signal processing for most of my career, at Boreal Photonics since 2011, and the Oulu photonics and RF engineering community is where I want to continue. That is the short version of why I am applying.

I have been looking for opportunities to make a more permanent move since, and Kaikuvaara’s posting is the first one that matches my background closely enough for a credible application.

My training at TU Maasdelta was in classical EE signal processing, and I have kept that foundation current through daily work at Boreal and through a retraining period I took in 2013–2014 to deepen my estimation theory and applied statistics knowledge. The Oulu engineering community, its scale and its focus, is a genuine draw. I am not someone who needs to be in Helsinki. I would rather be somewhere the engineering community is tight enough that you know the people doing interesting work, and Oulu is clearly that place.

I would be happy to discuss this further.

Anne Salminen

Dear Kaikuvaara,

For the past two and a half years at Fenno Radar Technologies I have been doing the kind of hands-on embedded signal processing work that your posting describes, and I want to explain why I am looking to move.

Fenno has been a strong first job out of university. I have written real-time DSP firmware in C++ for their X-band radar prototype, run hands-on RF measurements during the L-band phased-array prototype development, and worked on the motion compensation module for an airborne SAR project. The technical work has been exactly what I hoped for when I graduated from Oulu in 2023 — close to the hardware, demanding, and concrete. But Fenno is a small company with a narrow product focus, and after two and a half years the problems have started to feel familiar. I want to work on systems where the complexity keeps pushing me.

Kaikuvaara is interesting to me because the signal processing problems you describe are genuinely harder than what I currently face. The combination of phased-array work at scale, platform-level integration, and the real-time constraints of the systems you build is the kind of step up I am looking for. I have done beamforming design at Fenno and I know enough about the domain to understand that your work operates at a different level — the element counts, the bandwidths, the timing margins are all tighter than anything I have seen.

What I think I bring is direct, hands-on competence. Everything listed on my CV is work I did personally. I was at the bench with a vector network analyser, at a terminal writing timing-critical C++, and in the lab debugging real signal chains on actual hardware. I am not trying to manage my way into a senior role; I want to stay close to the technical core of the work, not drift from it.

My electrical engineering degree from the Oulujoki University gave me the signal processing theory I use daily — array processing, spectral analysis, waveform design — and two and a half years at Fenno have layered practical engineering judgment on top. I think the combination is worth more than either piece alone.

I am in Oulu already and can come in for a technical discussion whenever suits your schedule.

Jian Gupta
